name: Azure DevOps service-connection trust review
what: A read-first method to map who can turn an Azure DevOps pipeline into an Azure workload identity, then verify resource checks and narrow authorizations.
when: Before WIF migration, production pipeline onboarding, a project-scope change or investigation of suspicious workload identity use. Documentation-verified method; not lab-tested.
cost_note: The manual review method is free; Azure DevOps, agents, Azure resources and log ingestion can require paid services. No paid scanning product is required.
example: Get written scope and read access. List each production connection under `Project settings > Service connections`; record ID, identity IDs, authentication type, Azure role scope and owner. Never export secret values.

Record explicit pipeline authorizations, connection administrators, resource checks and bypass authorities. Flag `Grant access permission to all pipelines`; do not change it during the read-only inventory.

Trace the authorized pipeline to YAML/templates, repository policies, variable groups, environment and agent pool. Record who can edit each path and whether a self-hosted agent has another production identity or private-network route.
Have the Azure owner verify all identity grants, including Key Vault data access and inherited Azure RBAC. WIF does not remove excessive resource permissions.

Propose branch control on the actual credential resource, using fully qualified allowed branches and a deliberate unknown-protection decision. Propose independent approval and required templates where appropriate.

With separate change/test approval, validate allowed branch, disallowed branch and unauthorized-pipeline paths against a harmless target. Record fresh run IDs and target outcomes; the inventory alone changes nothing.

Keep a dated evidence matrix: connection → identity → target roles → authorized pipelines → checks → editors/administrators → agent trust. Store it in an approved private change record, with exceptions and review date.
pitfalls: An environment approval is not proof that every use of the service connection is gated. Review and protect the connection itself.
WIF eliminates a stored secret, not malicious code running in an authorized pipeline. Review issuer-side governance and Azure permissions together.
Resource administrators can bypass certain checks. A branch marked protected may have only one policy; validate the actual required review.
Keep this method read-only until the change owner approves a pilot; never make unreviewed production changes to prove a finding.
